correctness.rationale: The conic Q maps to H by the cubic coordinates identity; generic injectivity and pullback degree six prove finite birational normalization. Full gradient equations prove the four rational A1 nodes and six A2 cusps for every p>3. The node tangent discriminant is -3, so Frobenius fixes the two branches exactly when epsilon_p^r=1; cusps have residue-preserving single preimages. Counting q+1 on Q yields #H=q+1-4epsilon; the coordinate triangle has 3q rational points and meets H in exactly 3(1+eta) rational cusps. Inclusion-exclusion gives #D=4q-2-4epsilon-3eta and formal exp yields the zeta rational function. A standalone pure-Python independent polynomial enumerator passed 11 primes and 3 quadratic extensions. Universality relies on geometry, not finite samples.

value.rationale: Determines a natural complete arithmetic invariant—the Hasse–Weil zeta of a distinguished maximizing free divisor—and explains it by two different Frobenius splitting mechanisms. Rational nodes can have no rational normalization preimages; the normalization is a non-split real conic despite four real isolated nodes. These precise phenomena are unrecorded by the known characteristic-zero free exponents and have plausible use for studying arithmetic reduction of singular free divisors; no broader theory is asserted.
